label: nwpp 47 grid wind
definition: nwpp-47: serve GRID's pool-carried wind leg
market_story: The arm moves no mechanism of dispatch; it corrects what the footprint must serve. GRID (Gridforce) schedules a New Mexico wind farm whose output EIA-930 books in GRID and ships to PNM; the model's wind supply carries that wind from the pool series, so the export it feeds is real load on the footprint's supply. Serving it adds ~2 TWh/yr of requirement, which the marginal thermal units take exactly as the real Northwest system would at the margin: CC_REGULAR ~70-78% (the class setting the gas margin most hours), CT_PEAKER ~6-13% in peak hours, coal 3-16% where it has headroom. Hydro, wind, solar and nuclear do not move because their energy is fixed by water budgets and weather.
